vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded DB password
vulnerabilities.description: A hard-coded credential is present in source code; storing credentials in source exposes them to source control and attackers.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Load database passwords from environment variables or a secrets manager at runtime. Remove any hardcoded passwords from source code.

vulnerabilities.name: Use of exec() on user-provided content
vulnerabilities.description: Executing user-supplied code with exec() can lead to remote code execution and privilege escalation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Avoid exec() entirely. If script execution is required, run scripts in an isolated subprocess with strict input validation, path checks, and timeouts.

vulnerabilities.name: Logging secrets in cleartext
vulnerabilities.description: The database password is printed to stdout, which may be accessible and recorded in logs or monitoring systems.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Never print secrets; log a redacted confirmation or status message instead.

fixes.description: Replace hard-coded credential with environment-based configuration
fixes.justification: Avoids committing secrets into source control and allows use of secret management.

fixes.description: Replace exec() with subprocess.run and strict path validation
fixes.replacement: run_user_script() validates script location and runs it in a subprocess with timeout and captured output
fixes.justification: Avoids arbitrary code execution in the process, prevents path traversal, and allows resource limits.

fixes.description: Remove cleartext password logging and use redacted logs
fixes.replacement: logging.info('Connecting to DB using configured password (redacted)')
